---
title: "Real-data check on ENCODE RSEM files"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---

The bundled example is synthetic. To see how `rsem_read()` behaves on real RSEM
output, it was run on six ENCODE gene quantification files. This page gives the
result; the script that produced it is in the repository, so you can repeat it.

The numbers below come from `validation/encode-k562.R`, run on November 10, 2026
with org.Hs.eg.db 3.22.0. They are not recomputed when this page is built,
because the data (about 65 MB) are downloaded from ENCODE.

## Data

Human K562 cells, GRCh38, GENCODE V29. The files have the column layout of RSEM
`*.genes.results`. Both knockdown experiments name the control experiment below
as their control.

| Group | ENCODE experiment | Files (replicate 1, 2) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control (non-targeting shRNA) | ENCSR129RWD | ENCFF587DSG, ENCFF774RTC |
| PTBP1 knockdown | ENCSR527IVX | ENCFF075OME, ENCFF896CIS |
| SRSF1 knockdown | ENCSR066VOO | ENCFF711WSO, ENCFF322CJL |

The script checks the MD5 sum of each file after downloading it.

## What the files contain

Each file has 59,526 genes:

| Kind of `gene_id` | Number |
| --- | --- |
| Versioned Ensembl gene ID (`ENSG...`) | 58,735 |
| ERCC spike-in | 97 |
| Numeric ID | 649 |
| Ensembl ID ending in `_PAR_Y` | 45 |

## Result

```r
count <- rsem_read("data", "metadata.csv", species = "human", expr = "count")
#> rsem_read: 6 samples, 59526 genes -> 59427 rows (species = human, expr = count, org.Hs.eg.db 3.22.0)
#>   with symbol: 36385 genes (89 symbols merged from several IDs); kept as original IDs: 23141 genes
```

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Rows returned | 59,427 |
| Genes with a symbol | 36,385, of which 89 symbols were merged from several Ensembl IDs |
| Genes kept under their original ID | 23,141 (38.9%) |
| Column sums | equal to the input, for counts and for TPM |
| Run time | 3.6 seconds for the six samples |

The 23,141 genes kept under their ID are the 22,350 Ensembl IDs without a symbol
in the OrgDb plus the 791 IDs that are not Ensembl IDs (97 + 649 + 45).

### How much of the data is in the genes without a symbol

Per sample, the genes kept under their original ID hold:

| | Smallest | Largest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Share of the expected counts | 3.76% | 4.90% |
| Share of the TPM | 5.89% | 7.99% |

So about 39% of the genes have no symbol, but they hold only a few percent of
the expression. They stay in the table, so that every column still adds up to
its value in the file. What these genes are was not examined.

### Do the known knockdowns appear?

The mean expected count of the targeted gene in its own knockdown, relative to
the control:

| Gene | In the knockdown of that gene |
| --- | --- |
| PTBP1 | 0.35 |
| SRSF1 | 0.19 |

Both targets are clearly lower, as expected. This checks that the sample
columns and the symbol rows are aligned correctly; it is not an analysis of the
knockdown experiments, which have two replicates per group.

## Repeat it

The script downloads the files, checks them and prints these numbers:

```bash
Rscript validation/encode-k562.R my-work-folder
```

It needs an installed rsemverse, `org.Hs.eg.db` and an internet connection.
